subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In photography, 'cropping' an image means...
options: Cutting away parts of the frame to improve composition
questions.explain: Cropping removes unwanted edges to tighten or rebalance the composition.

questions.q: A 'hue' refers to which property of colour?
options: The pure colour itself, such as red or blue
questions.explain: Hue is the name of the pure colour, such as red, yellow or blue, before tints or shades are added.

questions.q: In a repeating textile print, the single unit that repeats is called the...
questions.explain: The motif is the design unit that is repeated across the fabric to form an all-over pattern.

questions.q: A graphic 'grid' is used to...
options: Organise and align text and images consistently
questions.explain: A grid provides an underlying structure that keeps elements aligned and the layout consistent.

questions.q: A 'mock-up' in graphic design is...
options: A finished printed product for sale
A trial version showing how a design will look
questions.explain: A mock-up is a realistic preview that shows how the final design will appear before production.

questions.q: A 'monochromatic' colour scheme uses...
options: Tints, tones and shades of a single colour
questions.explain: A monochromatic scheme uses one hue with its lighter tints and darker shades.

questions.q: The CMYK colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: CMYK (cyan, magenta, yellow, key/black) is the standard ink set used in colour printing.

questions.q: In weaving, the threads held under tension on the loom that run lengthways are the...
questions.explain: The warp threads run lengthways and are held taut on the loom while the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: What does 'firing' clay in a kiln do?
questions.explain: Firing heats clay to high temperatures, turning it permanently hard and durable.

questions.q: Which artist is most associated with Pop Art and images of soup cans?
questions.explain: Andy Warhol was a leading Pop Art figure, famous for his Campbell's soup can images.

questions.q: The sculpture technique of removing material from a solid block is called...
questions.explain: Carving is a subtractive method, cutting away material from a block of stone or wood.

questions.q: Salvador Dali is associated with which art movement?
questions.explain: Salvador Dali was a leading Surrealist, known for dream-like works such as his melting clocks.

questions.q: Frida Kahlo is best known for her...
questions.explain: Frida Kahlo is famous for intense, symbolic self-portraits drawing on her life and Mexican culture.

questions.q: In GCSE Art, the assessment objective about 'recording' asks you to...
options: Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to your intentions
Write an essay with no images
questions.explain: The recording objective is about capturing observations and ideas, for example through drawing and photography.

questions.q: What does adding white to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding white to a colour produces a tint (a lighter version), while adding black produces a shade.

questions.q: A 'pleat' is...
options: A stitched fold pressed into fabric to shape or decorate it
questions.explain: A pleat is a fold of fabric, often pressed and stitched, used to add shape or decoration.

questions.q: In film photography, in which room is light-sensitive paper developed?
questions.explain: Film and prints are processed in a darkroom, where safelight prevents the paper being fogged.

questions.q: A 'storyboard' is most useful for planning...
options: A sequence such as an animation or advert
questions.explain: A storyboard sketches a sequence of frames to plan how an animation or film will unfold.

questions.q: A graphite pencil labelled '6B' is...
questions.explain: The 'B' scale denotes softer, darker pencils, so 6B is much softer and darker than an H grade.

questions.q: The RGB colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: RGB (red, green, blue) is the additive light model used by screens and digital devices.

questions.q: 'Packaging' design must do all of these EXCEPT...
questions.explain: Packaging protects, informs and attracts, but it does not replace the product it contains.

questions.q: What is 'pattern' as a formal element?
options: The edge that defines a shape
A repeated arrangement of shapes, lines or colours
The lightness or darkness of an area
questions.explain: Pattern is created when elements such as shapes or marks are repeated in an organised way.
